questions.q: In a before trigger, how do you save a change to a field on the triggering record itself?
options: Set the field directly on the record in Trigger.new — no DML needed
Call Database.upsert
Call update on the record
Call insert again on the same record
questions.explain: Before triggers can modify Trigger.new directly; the platform persists those changes automatically when the save completes, with no extra DML call.

questions.q: Why is opp.Id null inside a before insert trigger but populated inside an after insert trigger?
options: Id is only ever set manually by the developer
Before triggers don't have access to Trigger.new at all
The record hasn't been committed to the database yet during the before phase, so no Id has been assigned
Id is a formula field recalculated only in after triggers
questions.explain: System-generated fields like Id only exist once the record is actually written to the database, which happens between the before and after phases.

questions.q: What does calling addError() on a field inside a before trigger do?
options: Logs a warning but still allows the save
Blocks the save and shows the message to the user
Deletes the record
Queues an asynchronous retry of the DML
questions.explain: addError() is how before triggers enforce validation in code — it halts the save and surfaces the message, similar to a declarative validation rule.

questions.q: Why do after triggers need an explicit DML statement to create a related Task, when before triggers don't need one to change their own fields?
options: After triggers are read-only by design
A Task is a separate record from the triggering record, so it must be explicitly inserted — only changes to the triggering record's own fields in a before trigger get auto-saved
DML is never required in any trigger phase
Tasks can only be created through Flow, never through Apex
questions.explain: The before-trigger auto-save behavior only applies to the record currently being processed; any other record, like a related Task, always needs its own DML statement.

questions.q: Which phase would you choose to default an Opportunity's CloseDate when it's left blank?
options: After update, with an explicit update statement
After insert, with an explicit update statement
After delete
Before insert, setting the field directly
questions.explain: Defaulting a field on the record being saved is exactly what before triggers are for — it avoids a second, unnecessary DML statement.
